title: Unveiling the power of Treg.Sig: a novel machine-learning derived signature for predicting ICI response in melanoma.
authors: Fan, Yunlong; Yang, Jiaman; Yang, Xin; Xie, Yulin; Li, Haiyang; Yang, Shuo; Sun, Guanchao; Ge, Ge; Ding, Xiao; Lai, Shengwei; Liao, Yong; Ji, Shuaifei; Yang, Rongya; Zhang, Xingyue
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习构建Treg相关基因签名预测黑色素瘤免疫治疗反应，核心是肿瘤免疫与临床预测，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) represents a significant breakthrough in cancer immunotherapy, only a few patients benefit from it. Given the critical role of Treg cells in ICI treatment resistance, we explored a Treg-associated signature in melanoma, which had never been elucidated yet. METHODS: A new Treg signature, Treg.Sig, was created using a computational framework guided by machine learning, utilizing transcriptome data from both single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-sequencing (bulk-seq). Among the 10 Treg.Sig genes, hub gene STAT1's function was further validated in ICI resistance in melanoma mice receiving anti-PD-1 treatment. RESULTS: Treg.Sig, based on machine learning, was able to forecast survival outcomes for melanoma across training dataset and external test dataset, and more importantly, showed superior predictive power than 51 previously established signatures. Analysis of the immune profile revealed that groups with high Treg.Sig levels exhibited immune-suppressive conditions, with inverse correlations observed between Treg.Sig and anti-cancer immune responses. Notably, among the 10 Treg.Sig genes, hub gene STAT1 mutation harbored lower response rate in ICIs-treated cohort. Mechanistically, STAT1 impinged on ICI resistances by modulating the phenotypic switch in N2 neutrophil polarization in melanoma mice receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, which affects overall survival. CONCLUSION: The study developed a promising Treg.Sig signature that predicts ICI response of melanomas and could be used for selecting patients for immunotherapy. Meanwhile, our study potentially paves the way for overcoming immune resistance by targeting Treg-associated genes.
abstract_zh: 背景：尽管免疫检查点抑制剂（immune checkpoint inhibitor, ICI）代表了癌症免疫治疗中的重大突破，但仅有少数患者从中获益。鉴于Treg细胞在ICI治疗耐药中的关键作用，我们探索了黑色素瘤中一种Treg相关特征，该特征此前尚未被阐明。方法：利用机器学习引导的计算框架，结合单细胞RNA测序（single-cell RNA-sequencing, scRNA-seq）和批量RNA测序（bulk RNA-sequencing, bulk-seq）的转录组数据，创建了一种新的Treg特征Treg.Sig。在10个Treg.Sig基因中，枢纽基因STAT1的功能在接受抗PD-1治疗的黑色素瘤小鼠的ICI耐药中得到了进一步验证。结果：基于机器学习的Treg.Sig能够预测训练数据集和外部测试数据集中黑色素瘤的生存结局，更重要的是，其预测能力优于51个先前建立的特征。免疫谱分析显示，Treg.Sig高表达组呈现免疫抑制状态，且Treg.Sig与抗癌免疫反应呈负相关。值得注意的是，在10个Treg.Sig基因中，枢纽基因STAT1突变在ICI治疗队列中表现出较低的缓解率。机制上，STAT1通过调节接受抗PD-1治疗的黑色素瘤小鼠中N2中性粒细胞极化的表型转换来影响ICI耐药，从而影响总生存期。结论：该研究开发了一种有前景的Treg.Sig特征，可预测黑色素瘤的ICI反应，并可用于选择免疫治疗患者。同时，我们的研究可能为通过靶向Treg相关基因克服免疫耐药铺平道路。
